reason: The cited implementation supports the revert on adding an unregistered EOA. However, concrete protocol impact and the binding status of the documentation statement remain unestablished.
caps: layers disagree: evidence requires E1 (obligation 3), the decision does not

evidence.claim: addRoleProvider calls IRoleProvider(providerAddress).isPullProvider() unconditionally, so an EOA provider (which has no code) causes the call to revert, contradicting the docs' statement that a role provider can be an EOA.
evidence.support_reason: At AccessControlHooks.sol:220 (and FixedTermLoanHooks.sol:257) addRoleProvider performs a high-level external call `IRoleProvider(providerAddress).isPullProvider()` whenever the provider is not already registered. Solidity's high-level call to an address with no code reverts (extcodesize check), so an EOA cannot be added as a new provider. Only the deployer, seeded in the constructor (lines 124-128 / 135-139), can be an EOA provider. The report's PoC trace matches this behavior.
preconditions: Borrower attempts to add an EOA as a role provider via addRoleProvider

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that the inability to add an EOA provider breaks a protocol invariant or causes loss, rather than only contradicting documentation prose
missing_evidence.why: The effect shown is a revert on a borrower configuration call; the docs statement is not a contest invariant, and the borrower can still use the deployer EOA or a contract provider, so the stated impact/severity is not established.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A concrete scenario is shown where the EOA-provider restriction causes loss of funds, DoS of a market function, or violation of a listed Main Invariant.

missing_evidence.item: Whether the docs statement 'a role provider can be an EOA' is a binding spec the contest treats as a vulnerability class
missing_evidence.why: The claim rests on documentation prose; the policy's known-issues/scope sections do not list this as in-scope, and the borrower is a trusted role who chooses providers, so the finding may be a design/documentation mismatch rather than an in-scope bug.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A cited contest policy clause or invariant establishes that EOA providers must be supported.
